# SK3004 — A `CancellationToken` is accepted and not passed on

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

A method takes a `CancellationToken` and calls something that offers an optional one without supplying it.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Async |
| Default severity | warning |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, review it |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 1.2 |

## Why

A cancellation token that stops at the first frame is a cancellation that does not happen. The caller sees the token accepted, assumes the operation is cancellable, and gets a request that runs to completion after the client has gone — which under load is how a server keeps working on answers nobody is waiting for. The chain has to be complete to be worth anything, and the place it breaks is always a call that offered the parameter and was not given it.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
async Task LoadAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken) {
    var text = await File.ReadAllTextAsync(path);
    await Task.Delay(100);
}
```

Write:

```csharp
async Task LoadAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken) {
    var text = await File.ReadAllTextAsync(path, cancellationToken);
    await Task.Delay(100, cancellationToken);
}
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **Only an *omitted optional* parameter is reported.** The called method must declare a `CancellationToken` parameter that has a default value and that this call site supplied no argument for, positionally or by name — so a method with no such parameter, an overload pair the rule would have to choose between, and a call that already passes a token are all invisible to it. A call that passes `CancellationToken.None` or `default` **explicitly** is left alone: writing the token out is how an author says the call is deliberately not cancellable, and a rule that overrides that is arguing with a decision rather than finding an omission. ⚠ **Calls inside a `catch` or a `finally` are excluded**, because cleanup that a cancellation can abort is worse than cleanup that ignores it, and that is where the exception is legitimate. Test methods are excluded for the same reason `SK3002` excludes them. The enclosing body must have exactly one `CancellationToken` in scope; with two, which one to forward is a question the rule cannot answer, so it does not ask it. The fix appends a **named** argument, which is correct whether or not the intervening optional parameters were supplied, and is marked unsafe because passing a token makes a call cancellable that previously was not — a behaviour change the author should see.
